q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM (SELECT CLASS , COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) AS A FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS) AS T WHERE A>=5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM (SELECT CLASS , COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) AS A FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS) AS T WHERE A>=5
explanation: Q1 groups by CLASS and checks if the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class is >= 5. Q2 first groups by CLASS and counts the distinct students in each class, then filters for classes where this count is >= 5. The difference lies in how Q2 handles duplicate student entries within the same class.
counterexample_dsp: A class with 5 students, where 4 of them are the same student (i.e., 4 duplicate entries for the same student). Q1 will count this as 5 students in the class, satisfying the condition. Q2, however, will count only 2 distinct students (the unique student and the duplicate), not satisfying the condition.
